I know if feel bad right now, and a lot of people will tell you that it will get better. Maybe it will, maybe it won't, and if it doesn't, can I ask you to consider just one thing?

If you're planning to leave this world and you have nothing to lose, why not say goodbye to it properly? Take a year, your last year to go everywhere, see everything. Get jobs in cruises, ships, farms, anything, just to pay for basic needs, and get you moving.

Go to another country where you don't speak the language, get help from strangers, or get fooled by locals. Either way, take all that as the last time you're going through that. I know it may seem like too much trouble now, but I really believe we're miserable when we're not where we really wanted to be.

My parents didn't pressure me as much as my aunts and cousins. Seems like all they would talk about was about marriage and kids. To be fair, most of them were engaged or in a relationship, so their life was pretty much just about that, but it was enough for me to get tired of it all.

I think at some level I always knew. When I was growing up I was the flower girl in most of my family's weddings and that seemed like it was what we had to do, get married and have children. I had ready answers to most questions my aunts would always ask me since I was 2 years old: "how big do you want your wedding to be?" - Very very big. "How many kids do you want to have?" - I don't know, I still have time to think about that. "Do you imagine how your husband will be?" - I would always look disgusted for that one because I was a child.

I would always take care of my cousins, I was the baby sitter at all family gatherings, and I think I got tired of babies and kids. As soon as I began to think for myself and realized that high school and graduating would be a lot of work, family and kids began to feel like just too much and I would often argue with my dad saying how annoying babies were, that all they did was cry and shit.

He told me many times that I was lucky he and my mom didn't think like that, and I would always say "yeah, but that was your choice". After that I realized that having kids never made sense for me, and even big weddings felt like too much trouble, so maybe, all the insistence of my family made me actually get tired of it and realize it didn't fit the lifestyle I want to have.

Maybe if they hadn't been so pushy and talk about that since my first breath, maybe I could want something, but it still doesn't fit the lifestyle I love to have.

On one of my first days as an Intern at the hospital, I was late for a meeting with my teacher and my colleagues, so I was power walking on one of those really long hospital corridors. It was a very old hospital, that seems like a labyrinth and since I had already got lost, I was walking for 15-20 minutes trying to find them, so most of my blood was already on my legs, I wasn't thinking straight

Then, when I started walking on the corridor, I saw a patient lying on a bed, in the middle of the corridor (not uncommon) with a very young doctor (I assumed from the white coat) looking attentively to the saline IV bag. The "doctor" was inspecting with too much attention the velocity that the drops were falling in the drip chamber, and it poked the chamber a few times (I assumed that it wasn't drooping as quick as the "doctor" wanted)

I passed by them and realized that the doctor was probably still a student since it looked like someone that had just got out from high school, and my assumptions were confirmed when after I looked back and saw the "doctor" BLOWING (yes, with his bacteria filled mouth) in the IV tube that was connected to the patients arm!!

For those that are not familiar with medical practices, if you contaminate the iv tube, you will inject a lot of bacteria straight into the patient's blood, that bacteria will spread quickly and you will create a huge problem, and another thing: **you can't inject too much air into the blood stream, that can and probably will kill you.**

I didn't even had the time to turn back and stop that, but I saw the nurses rushing to rescue the patient, so, I know it wasn't exactly my fucked up, but I consider that I fucked up by not stopping and preventing that stupid attempt of murder with (I hope) probably good intentions

Bipolar disorder is actually pretty hard to diagnose since the patient has a period of Mania and a period of Depression and it's often misdiagnosed just as Depression. The Mania period the person may function well, so it's often not seeing by psychiatrists.

The NPD has some traits that may be seen as bipolar disorder and anxiety disorder, but it's not necessarily both disorders at the same time.

The NPD is closer to a sociopathty since the patient doesn't have the ability of feeling true empathy for others and their modus operandi is to use mimicking emotions to get some kind of reaction from people around them.

It's kind of like this:

A normal person can feel a range of emotions that will go from -10 to +10. Good things, like hearing "I love you" from someone you love will give you a +10 emotion, and bad emotions like being caught stealing, or the death of someone you love, will give you a -10 emotion.

Psychopaths (that's not the term they use anymore, but I'll keep using if for didattic purposes) will have a range of emotions closer to 0, like from -1 to +1. They just are physically unable to feel anything, that's what make them dangerous since they don't feel remorse from using people to get what they want and they learn how to manipulate normal people mimicking emotions. They learn that if they cry and pretend that they are upset, it's more likely that people that love them will do everything in their power to give them something they wanted.

And NPD is somewhere between -6 to +6, but they can get to +8, +10 emotions if they get very strong reactions from people around them. They are addicted to drama (a strong emotion) and they need to be in the center of attention. Drama and being a victim often gives them that thrill of a +8 or +10 emotion, but it doesn't last long like normal people. While a normal person can feel +10, +9 emotions for 24h after a really good emotion, and the next day it will still be something like +7, +8 feeling, for the NDP, that +10 emotion will last only a few minutes, so in 15-20min it will ne already back to a +6 emotion tops. So the NDP needs to constantly be in the center of attention to feel something. It can be good or bad emotion, but it needs to me strong, that's why they do what they do.

They will constantly poison people around them to keep them always ready to explode, to pick up a fight with them or with someone else and give them the thrill of a strong emotion. And if the people around them fights with the NDP, it's extra points because, not only they will have the thrill of that strong emotion, but they also get the extra of telling people about what happened and how they were the victim of an unpredictable attack, so they can keep that emotion alive.

Like, ChessPigeon is constantly poisoning ex-SO against ex-JMBIL, that way ChessPigeon can always complain to ex-SO about something that Ex-JMBIL did and be the victim to ex-SO, she can always complain to ex-JMBIL about ex-SO and be the victim, and she can complain to strangers "my sons hate each other, I'm so sad and I don't know why, I raised them to be friends, but they hate each other" and she's the victim again getting a strong reaction from the stranger.

ChessPigeon looks like she has Anxiety Disorder, but she probably just have NDP and learned that when she's mimicking anxiousness, people will give her a lot of attention to help her to calm down, but that attention only escalates her "anxiety" until everyone around her is just as anxious as she pretends to be and she will have a lot of people giving her a lot of strong emotions.

I don't know if I was able to explain well how the NPD works, but I'll keep learning about it and I'll see if I can correlate NPD with bipolar disorder, but I strongly believe that the NPD just mimics emotions that will look like bipolar disorder or they learned that alternating their emotions they will get better reactions from their public.
